The essay runs to roughly five pages and carries no section headings; the review reconstructs it as eight numbered movements with page anchors, then separates nine prescriptive…

items.summary: Recursive Risk and the Babel Archetype: Why Unbounded Artificial Superintelligence Threatens Human Control The rapid acceleration of artificial intelligence research has shifted the prospect of Artificial Superintelligence (ASI)—an intellect vastly superior to human cognitive performance across all domains—from theoretical speculation to an active engineering goal. This paper presents a counter-narrative to the prevailing technological optimism surrounding ASI. Drawing upon foundational principles in AI safety, cybernetic systems theory, and the cultural archetype of the Tower of Babel, this research argues that humanity must not engineer an autonomous entity it cannot control. items.title: Moral Formation Architectures for Artificial Superintelligence: A Research Prospectus
items.summary: Abstract Contemporary AI governance frameworks focus predominantly on evaluation, monitoring, resilience, auditing, and mitigation after advanced capabilities emerge. While these approaches are important and necessary, they generally begin after powerful capabilities already exist. This prospectus proposes that a developmental layer may be largely absent from current AI governance discussions. Specifically, it explores whether advanced intelligence should undergo structured moral formation during model gestation and development prior to deployment. The paper introduces the concept of moral formation architectures and argues that developmental formation may represent a high-leverage…

items.title: GenNA: Conditional generation of nucleotide sequences guided by natural language annotations
items.summary: Deciphering the mapping between biomolecular sequences and complex biological functions is a central challenge in genomics. While existing generative nucleotide models capture sequence distributions, they lack explicit access to gene-associated biological semantics, limiting semantics-guided design. Here, we present GenNA, a generative nucleotide foundation model guided by natural language annotations. Pretrained on a multimodal nucleotide-text corpus spanning 2221 eukaryotic species (∼416 billion characters), GenNA internalizes relationships between sequence syntax and functional semantics within a unified autoregressive framework. Without explicit rule-based supervision, GenNA yields…

items.title: Unlocking the Activities of Polyglutamylation Enzymes in Brain Tubulin With Top‐Down Mass Spectrometry
items.summary: Microtubules, essential components of the cytoskeleton, are formed from α- and β-tubulin heterodimers which are organized in a cylindrical fashion. The carboxy-terminal tubulin tails are exposed on the outside of the microtubule, where they can be highly modified by post-translational modifications (PTMs). One PTM, polyglutamylation, consists in the addition and extension of glutamate chains and is catalyzed by tubulin tyrosine ligase-like (TTLL) enzymes. In mice, TTLL1 and TTLL7 are two key polyglutamylases in neurons, leading to high levels of polyglutamylation on both α- and β-tubulin. Here we purified tubulin from wild-type, Ttll1-knockout (Ttll1-KO), Ttll7-knockout (Ttll7-KO), and…

items.title: A new method to probe conducting filaments in MoS 2 -based memristors
items.summary: Abstract Two-dimensional (2D) transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs), such as molybdenum disulfide (MoS₂), are emerging as promising materials for next-generation electronic devices. They have proved to be serious candidates for integration with memristors in non-volatile memory and radio frequency (RF) applications. However, the physical mechanisms behind their resistive switching, particularly the formation and resorption of conducting filaments, remain unclear. In this study, we present a novel mechanical exfoliation technique that selectively removes the top metallic electrode from MoS₂-based memristors by exploiting the weak van der Waals interaction between MoS₂ and the top…

items.summary: We present an exploration-first strategy for intramolecular conformational search. Because practical quantum-chemical (QC) models are approximate, candidate retention combines energy and interaction descriptors as separate objectives, while structural diversity is preserved until post-search reduction. The SEEKER (Structural Ensemble Exploration through Knowledge-Guided Evaluation and Routing) program explores explicitly declared acyclic torsions through unit-quaternion rotations while retaining fixed ring families. We assess reference-set coverage for amino acids, the sugars D-glucose, erythrulose, and fructose, and thiopronine using per-reference nearest-candidate heavy-atom…

items.title: Hyperbolic neural networks for biologically informed classification of white blood cells and hematopoietic cell states in peripheral blood smears
items.summary: Abstract Automated white blood cell (WBC) classification in peripheral blood smears supports morphological assessment of hematological disorders, but most deep learning classifiers treat cell categories as independent labels and do not account for hematopoietic maturation. We propose a hyperbolic classification framework that combines a ResNet-18 feature extractor with a prototype-based classifier in the Poincaré ball, allowing biologically related cell states to be represented in a geometry suited to hierarchical structure. The model was evaluated on a curated dataset of 129,174 annotated single-cell images mapped to 14 blood cell classes, including leukocyte subtypes, hematopoietic…

items.title: Pelorus: Warped-Product Graph Indexing for Hyperbolic Vector Search
items.summary: Hyperbolic embeddings capture hierarchical relations, but million-scale approximate nearest neighbor search must reconcile geodesic fidelity with memory efficiency. Flat inner-product indices distort order across radial shells, while native hyperbolic graphs repeatedly access full-precision vectors or quantize coordinates with singular conformal scales. We present Pelorus, a warped-product proximity-graph index for hyperbolic vector search. Pelorus separates unquantized FP32 radial and conformal scalars from scale-invariant 2-bit spherical directional codes and defers full-vector FP64 evaluation to a compact reranking tail. A conformal distortion analysis motivates orthogonal-projection…

items.title: LoopROS: A Dual Recursive Self-Improvement Loops of Robotic Operating System Based on Functional Constraints and Trajectory Tuning
items.summary: Recent advances in foundation models have enabled robotic agents to reason, plan, and adapt their actions through physical interaction. Yet successful execution does not necessarily translate into lasting improvement across tasks. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) offers a promising paradigm for robotic agents to continuously refine their capabilities through experience, but requires preserving functional knowledge, adapting execution to changing physical conditions, and retaining reusable corrections. We introduce LoopROS, a dual-loop robotic agent framework that couples functionally constrained execution with experience-driven improvement. Within each episode, functional constraint-guided…

items.title: SEA-Lab: Experiment-grounded recursive self-improvement in an automated laboratory
items.summary: AI scientists can generate hypotheses, plans, and protocols. Translating these outputs into reliable experiments requires adapting them to local equipment and resources using feedback from observed outcomes. A key challenge is to retain laboratory execution feedback as reusable knowledge for subsequent planning. We present SEA-Lab (Self-Evolving Autonomous Lab), which combines an environment-grounded Dry-Lab Harness that generates protocols and machine-readable procedures, a wet-lab execution harness that coordinates heterogeneous devices and records execution traces and experimental measurements, and a recursive self-improvement mechanism that uses physical feedback to revise reusable…

items.summary: Degenerate horizons of black holes surrounded by a Kiselev quintessence fluid open into two product throats: a Nariai region dS2 × S2$ when the black-hole and cosmological horizons merge, and a Bertotti–Robinson region AdS2 × S2 when the charged hole becomes extremal. These separable charts of constant curvature reduce the field equation to one Lamé equation read on two lines of a complex torus. items.title: Effect of xanthan gum on 3D-printed dysphagia foods.
items.summary: Background The global trend of population ageing is progressively worsening, leading to an increasing prevalence of dysphagia among the elderly population. Meanwhile, 3D printing technology offers a viable solution by providing customized, nutrient-rich, dysphagia-friendly foods for affected individuals. This study utilized Pleurotus ostreatus mycelium (POM), xanthan gum (XG), and egg white protein as primary materials. Building upon previous research investigating the impact of POM on 3D-printed dysphagia-friendly foods, this study investigates the feasibility of developing such foods via 3D printing by varying the concentration of XG (0, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90 g kg -1 ). items.title: Addressable Control of Hybrid Spin Qubit in Single-Atom Copper-Modified Fullerene.
items.summary: Developing high-dimensional solid-state quantum technologies requires overcoming the trade-off between spin dimensionality and quantum coherence. Hybrid spin architectures offer a promising solution to expand the quantum state space bottom-up by combining rapid electronic manipulation with robust nuclear phase memory. However, solid-state hybrid spin materials capable of simultaneously supporting both electron and nuclear spin manipulations remain exceedingly rare. Here, we report a Cu2+ (S = 1/2, I = 3/2) hybrid spin system dispersed in a magnetically silent C60 matrix, in which we not only demonstrate comprehensive coherent control over both electron and nuclear spin degrees of freedom…

items.title: Projected Korteweg stresses and fluctuation-induced viscosities: the role of order-parameter conservation.
items.summary: We calculate fluctuation-induced contributions to the shear and configurational bulk viscosities arising from Korteweg stresses in a Gaussian scalar-field theory. Starting from the Ginzburg-Landau functional, we derive the stress tensor and examine its gauge freedom. The longitudinal stress is then subjected to the Mori projection. items.title: Where the Loop Meets the Budget: Analyzing On-Device Recursive Self-Improvement
items.summary: Persistent self-improvement enables language-model agents to adapt from experience, but its update process competes with inference for limited device memory, energy, and thermal headroom. Existing surveys largely examine self-improvement mechanisms and on-device learning separately, providing limited guidance on how update reliability and device costs should be assessed together. We introduce a unified taxonomy that organizes persistent updates by component, execution locus, feedback, loop closure, timescale, and budget, and distinguishes recursive changes to evaluators or update machinery. Across the included works, we compare updates to memory and skills, prompts and code, weights, and…

items.title: Integration and annotation of spatial multi-omic data with DIRAC.
items.summary: Spatial multi-omic technologies measure multiple molecular layers within intact tissues. Two central challenges are vertical integration, which combines different molecular modalities, and horizontal integration, which aligns cell types across studies. Here we show domain invariant representation through adaptive calibration (DIRAC), a geometric deep learning model that unifies these tasks in a generalized domain adaptation framework. DIRAC learns task-discriminative features that are insensitive to domain shifts caused by batch effects, omic modalities or study sites, enabling a shared embedding space and automated cell-type annotation through label transfer from reference datasets.…

items.title: When, Where, and How Experience Becomes Structure: Mechanisms for Recursive Self-Improvement in LLM Agents
items.summary: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) studies how AI systems modify themselves and carry those changes into the generation of subsequent improvements. LLM agents can pursue this process by using interaction experience to revise Prompt, Memory, Skill, and Harness in some cases while keeping the task-execution model’s weights fixed. However, execution feedback does not directly specify which component should change, and a locally successful revision may not remain useful across tasks or subsequent improvement cycles. Understanding how experience becomes persistent agent structure therefore requires examining when evidence justifies a change, where that change should act, and how it is…

items.title: Learning inhibitor interactions from protein deep mutational scanning data and deep learning models
items.summary: Recent advances in protein language models, geometric deep learning, and structure prediction frameworks have the potential to accelerate computational drug discovery. However, it remains unclear how well these methods generalize beyond their training sets. Mutation-dependent drug responses present a challenge to these methods because there are often large effects from relatively small perturbations. Here, we systematically benchmark diverse mutational effect and drug-target affinity prediction models using deep mutational scanning datasets spanning 11 inhibitor conditions for the MET kinase domain. Across both mutational effect prediction and drug–target affinity tasks, current AI models…

items.title: From Harness Optimization to Recursive Self-Improvement: A Survey of Language Model Agents
items.summary: Language-model agents rely on harnesses that govern tool use, context, memory, and execution. Understanding automated harness revision requires connecting improvement methods to the reusable functionality they produce. This survey examines three linked perspectives: improvement workflows, recursive scope, and concrete modifications across task domains. We compare search strategies, memory management, edit guidance, and integration with model training, and use an existing five-level framework to distinguish harness optimization from recursive self-improvement. Across coding, reasoning and information processing, interactive and embodied tasks, and visual tasks, we trace reported changes…

items.title: AI4AI: Toward AI-Discovered Superintelligence
items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping how AI itself is developed. From designing learning algorithms to automating research workflows and evaluation, this expanding role has fueled the rapid growth of AI for AI (AI4AI). Yet a fundamental question remains: as AI takes on more research tasks, which decisions does it actually control? Even systems that execute entire research workflows may still rely on humans to define research goals, allowable modifications, and criteria for success. Existing taxonomies, typically organized by technique or target artifact, offer limited insight into these differences in research responsibility. This survey presents a unified, control-centered…

items.title: Recursive Self Improvement for Embodied Agents—A Survey of Foundations Mechanisms Harnesses and Evaluation
items.summary: Embodied foundation models have expanded robot capabilities, but autonomous execution does not automatically provide autonomous improvement. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) concerns retained changes that can influence subsequent improvement, including the stronger case in which an agent revises the procedures that generate and evaluate future updates. This survey connects large-model learning and reasoning, agent memory and skills, and RSI theory. We compare general agent harnesses with embodied harnesses and organize the literature along four axes: improvement targets, update mechanisms, decision authority and evidence conditions. The method review covers reflection and knowledge…
